title: In the Car Sticker

description.main: Die-cut metallic sticker of Roy Lichtenstein's In the Car (1963), made by the Brooklyn studio Apply under license from the artist's estate and sold by the Whitney Museum shop.
description.extended:
A die-cut sticker of Roy Lichtenstein's In the Car (1963), one of the romance-comic paintings of his first Pop years, produced by the Brooklyn studio Apply and sold by the Whitney Museum shop.

Screen-printed on metallic poly and die-cut to the image, the sticker measures 3 by 2.6 inches. It reproduces the painting's blonde woman in a leopard coat and dark-haired man at the wheel, with speed lines across the window, a composition Lichtenstein took from a romance-comic panel. Apply made it under license from the Estate of Roy Lichtenstein as one of four Lichtenstein stickers. The Whitney stocked the set in 2026 ahead of its retrospective Roy Lichtenstein: Like New (October 11, 2026 to May 10, 2027).

Lichtenstein (1923-1997) arrived at his signature manner in 1961: subjects lifted from comic strips and advertisements, painted in flat colour with hand-drawn Benday dots. By 1964 he was among the most recognised and most contested of the Pop artists. The Whitney holds 460 of his works, including the Roy Lichtenstein Study Collection given by the artist's foundation.

notes: Screen-printed on metallic poly, dishwasher safe. Copyright line: 2024, Estate of Roy Lichtenstein. Acquired from the Whitney Museum Shop: https://shop.whitney.org/products/lichtenstein-in-the-car-sticker
